title: Unraveling Diabetic Neuropathy in Mexico: From Diagnostic Challenges to an Uncertain Reported Prevalence
content: Diabetic neuropathy is one of the most common diabetes-related complications but also one of the most complex in terms of diagnosis and management. This complication refers to a heterogeneous group of peripheral nerve disorders resulting from a combination of metabolic, vascular, and neurodegenerative factors, typically triggered by chronic hyperglycemia, which has a significant impact on quality of life. Despite its clinical relevance, the diagnosis of diabetic neuropathy remains challenging due to its diverse clinical manifestations and the lack of a single diagnostic approach capable of identifying all diabetic neuropathy types. Available diagnostic approaches range from clinical assessment and symptom-based scales to neurophysiological and small-fiber-specific techniques, each with distinct diagnostic performance and methodological requirements. Consequently, reported prevalence estimates may vary considerably among populations and studies. In Mexico, this variability is particularly relevant, as the prevalence of diabetic neuropathy has been reported across a wide range, making it difficult to establish a reliable national estimate. Differences in study populations, diagnostic criteria, and assessment methods may substantially contribute to this heterogeneity.
